Storage pilot begins operating

The pilot project began operating this week at a wind farm on the coast. Engineers said the system had passed its first set of tests and would now run under normal grid conditions for two years.

The operator described the trial as a way to learn how long-duration storage behaves over several seasons, including periods of low wind that last for days. It will publish a summary of the results after the first year.

Local officials welcomed the project and said it could lead to a larger installation if the trial meets its targets. No date has been set for a decision on a second phase, and the operator said costs would decide the timing.

Independent analysts noted that similar pilots elsewhere had taken longer than planned to reach full output, and that the first months of data would show whether the design copes with cold weather.
